items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: I actually quoted the final strain to “El Capitan” by Sousa in this thing

ctx.x: How did your music experience in the public school system affect you? Was it okay or did you kind of —

It was okay. I remember in grammar school there was a little old, Earl Barry, he was a violin player actually. A nice little old man with a moustache and we had a silly little band made up of around 19 violins, 4 or 5 mandolins, 3 or 4 or 5 maybe accordions, a bunch of metal clarinets, and a drummer and me. And that was what the band was. And oddly enough I actually wrote in the seventh grade, I wrote the “Niantic School March,” which we played of course. I wrote it out and he transcribed it the way he thought I…
Hey, he might have saved you from getting arrested.
